title: Thy Works, Not Mine, O Christ
description: Thy Works, Not Mine, O Christ in Tonic Solfa to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR), doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Horatius Bonar wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 329.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR); any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy works, not mine, O Christ, Speak glad-ness to this heart; They tell me all is done, They bid my fear de-part. To whom, save Thee, who canst a-lone For sin a-tone, Lord, shall I flee?

lines: Thy works, not mine, O Christ,
Speak gladness to this heart;
They tell me all is done,
They bid my fear depart.
To whom, save Thee, who canst alone
For sin atone, Lord, shall I flee?
Thy cross, not mine, O Christ,
Has borne the awful load
Of sins that none in heaven
Or earth could bear but God.
To whom, save Thee, who canst alone
For sin atone, Lord, shall I flee?
Thy death, not mine, O Christ,
Has paid the ransom due;
Ten thousand deaths like mine
Would have been all too few.
To whom, save Thee, who canst alone
For sin atone, Lord, shall I flee?
Thy righteousness, O Christ,
Alone can cover me;
No righteousness avails
Save that which is of Thee.
To whom, save Thee, who canst alone
For sin atone, Lord, shall I flee?

licence: Public domain: Horatius Bonar died in 1889.
credits: Words by Horatius Bonar (1808–1889), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to ST. JOHN (PARISH CHOIR) by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
